articles.title: Fábio Trad apresenta propostas para educação e professores em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato ao governo de Mato Grosso do Sul participou de encontro com trabalhadores da educação nesta quarta-feira (16), em Campo Grande, e também falou sobre ensino técnico, evasão escolar e acesso à universidade.
articles.summary: Fábio Trad defende equiparação salarial de docentes, climatização de escolas e expansão do ensino técnico em encontro com educadores de Mato Grosso do Sul.
articles.body:
Fábio em agenda nesta quarta-feira (16) — Foto: Gabi Cenciarelli

O candidato ao governo de Mato Grosso do Sul Fábio Trad (PT) apresentou propostas para professores, escolas e estudantes durante encontro com trabalhadores da educação durante agenda nesta quarta-feira (16), na sede da Federação dos Trabalhadores em Educação de Mato Grosso do Sul (Fetems), em Campo Grande .

Entre as propostas apresentadas estão a equiparação dos salários de professores contratados e concursados, formação continuada e uma política de atenção à saúde mental dos profissionais. Trad também defendeu gratificações para professores que concluírem doutorado.

“Primeiro, nós vamos equiparar o salário dos professores contratados e dos professores concursados. [...] Vamos dar formação continuada e vamos dar maiores gratificações àqueles que concluírem doutorado”, afirmou.

Durante a agenda, Trad cumprimentou apoiadores, conversou com trabalhadores da educação e subiu ao palco acompanhado da candidata a vice. O candidato disse que participou do encontro também para ouvir sugestões da categoria e incorporá-las ao programa de governo.

Para a estrutura das escolas, Fábio Trad disse que pretende investir em climatização das salas de aula, segurança, alimentação, transporte, acesso à internet e laboratórios de informática e tecnologia.

“Nós queremos escolas com as salas climatizadas, escolas seguras, com alimentação de qualidade e transporte de qualidade, e todas as escolas com internet e laboratório de informática e tecnologia”, disse.

O candidato também afirmou que pretende universalizar gradualmente o ensino em tempo integral.

“Nós vamos universalizar o ensino integral gradualmente, mas ensino integral com qualidade, com professores valorizados, bem remunerados”, afirmou.

Trad também propôs um programa para identificar, no início do ano letivo, estudantes com baixo aproveitamento. Segundo o candidato, a medida teria como objetivo reduzir a evasão no ensino médio.

Para o ensino médio, Trad defendeu que a formação dos estudantes seja adequada à vocação econômica de cada região de Mato Grosso do Sul. Segundo a proposta apresentada pelo candidato, os cursos técnico-profissionalizantes seriam oferecidos por universidades públicas e institutos federais.

“Nós temos que adaptar o ensino médio à vocação econômica de cada região. E quem vai fornecer os cursos técnico-profissionalizantes serão as universidades públicas e os institutos federais”, afirmou.

Sobre o acesso ao ensino superior, Fábio Trad disse que pretende fomentar a criação de cursinhos populares para preparar estudantes que querem ingressar em universidades.

Ao fim da agenda, o candidato afirmou que o programa de governo está aberto a novas propostas apresentadas pela categoria.

“Além de apresentar as propostas, eu venho ao vivo porque o nosso programa de governo é constantemente dinâmico, está em um lugar para incorporar novas propostas que valorizem os professores, os alunos e as escolas públicas”, disse.

Os demais candidatos não enviaram suas agendas dentro do prazo estipulado.

articles.title: Éguas atravessam rodovia, atingem veículo e são capturadas em Arraial | G1
articles.standfirst: Animais foram encontrados nos bairros Sabiá e Caiçara após denúncias de moradores.
articles.summary: Animais foram encontrados nos bairros Sabiá e Caiçara após denúncias de moradores.
articles.body:
Éguas capturadas em Arraial do Cabo — Foto: Prefeitura de Arraial do Cabo

Duas éguas foram capturadas nesta quarta-feira (16) nos bairros Sabiá e Caiçara, em Arraial do Cabo , na Região dos Lagos, após moradores denunciarem a presença de animais soltos em vias públicas. A ação foi realizada pelo Grupamento de Apreensão de Animais da Secretaria Municipal de Segurança Pública.

Segundo os agentes, as éguas atravessavam a rodovia e espalhavam lixo pelas ruas, o que representava risco para motoristas, pedestres e para os próprios animais.

Em uma das ocorrências, o animal atingiu o veículo de um morador. Não foram divulgadas informações sobre feridos ou a dimensão dos danos causados.

O Grupamento de Apreensão de Animais informou que funciona 24 horas e realizará operações semanais nos distritos do município.

Casos de cavalos soltos podem ser comunicados ao Centro Integrado de Operações de Segurança Pública pelo telefone (22) 99700-0387.

articles.title: Univasf abre inscrições para mestrado e doutorado em Petrolina | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao todo, são ofertadas 59 vagas, sendo 27 para o mestrado e 32 para o doutorado. Interessados devem se inscrever até o dia 30 pela internet.
articles.summary: A Univasf recebe inscrições para 59 vagas de mestrado e doutorado em ciências da saúde e biológicas até o dia 30 de maio pelo site oficial.
articles.body:
Univasf Campus Petrolina — Foto: Emerson Rocha / g1 Petrolina

Estão abertas as inscrições para o mestrado e doutorado acadêmico em ciências da saúde e biológicas da Universidade Federal do Vale do São Francisco ( Univasf ), no Campus Sede, em Petrolina , no Sertão de Pernambuco. Os interessados podem se inscrever até a quinta-feira (30), exclusivamente por meio de formulário eletrônico (clique aqui) .

Ao todo, são ofertadas 59 vagas, sendo 27 para o mestrado e 32 para o doutorado, distribuídas entre ampla concorrência e modalidades de reserva de vagas.

Podem participar do processo para mestrado candidatos com diploma de graduação reconhecido pelo MEC, licenciatura ou bacharelado. E portadores de diploma ou declaração de conclusão de curso de mestrado, para concluintes de pós-graduação nível mestrado, para interssados em doutorado. Os documentos necessários estão disponíveis no edital .

O processo seletivo será composto por quatro fases: prova objetiva de conhecimentos em ciências da saúde e biológicas; enquadramento de projetos de pesquisa; defesa e arguição de projeto; e análise de currículo.

A prova objetiva será eliminatória e classificatória e terá aplicação presencial, em 16 de outubro, a partir das 14h, com duração de duas horas. A prova será aplicada simultaneamente no campus sede, em Petrolina, e no campus Senhor do Bonfim . O candidato deverá indicar o local de realização da prova no momento da inscrição.

A segunda fase, de enquadramento de projetos de pesquisa, será eliminatória e avaliará a aderência do projeto aos projetos de pesquisa do orientador indicado, além da interdisciplinaridade da proposta. A defesa e argumentação do projeto será eliminatória e classificatória, de forma remota, entre 9 e 13 de novembro deste ano.

A análise de currículo será classificatória e terá como base o currículo Lattes e a produção acadêmica referente ao período de 2022 a 2026, conforme o barema estabelecido no edital. O resultado final do processo seletivo está previsto para ser divulgado em 9 de dezembro, e a homologação do resultado pelo colegiado do programa para o dia 8 de dezembro.

Mais informações podem ser adquiridas pelo e-mail cpgcsb@univasf.edu.br .

articles.title: Radares de velocidade média: como funcionam os testes na BR-050 | G1
articles.standfirst: O sistema cruza a distância entre os dois pontos com o tempo levado pelo veículo para percorrê-la, sendo possível saber se o motorista andou acima da média em trecho sem radar.
articles.summary: Radares de velocidade média calculam o tempo de percurso entre dois pontos na BR-050 e, durante os testes da ANTT, terão caráter educativo sem multas.
articles.body:
Trecho da BR-050, em Uberaba — Foto: Reprodução/TV Integração

A Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT) autorizou testes de um novo sistema de controle de velocidade média em rodovias federais concedidas que cortam Minas Gerais. A BR-050, que passa por Uberaba , no Triângulo Mineiro, terá trecho monitorado.

Também haverá testes na BR-040, na BR-381 e BR-116. A iniciativa foi autorizada pela Superintendência de Infraestrutura Rodoviária (Surod) da ANTT em decisões publicadas no Diário Oficial da União em 11 de setembro.

A diferença para os radares tradicionais está no modo como a velocidade é calculada. Em vez de registrar apenas a velocidade de um veículo ao passar por determinado ponto, o sistema acompanha o tempo que ele leva para percorrer um trecho entre dois pontos de monitoramento. A partir da distância e do tempo de percurso, é calculada a velocidade média.

Apesar dos equipamentos já terem sido autorizados, os testes não começaram no dia da publicação das decisões. Segundo a ANTT, os 180 dias de experimento passam a ser contados a partir da efetiva implantação dos equipamentos e do início do monitoramento em cada trecho.

A ANTT poderá ainda prorrogar ou encerrar antecipadamente os testes mediante decisão fundamentada da Surod.

O g1 questionou a Eco-050, concessionária responsável pelo trecho, sobre a data de implantação dos radares, mas não obteve resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Na BR-050/MG, o projeto-piloto será realizado entre os quilômetros 171 e 270 e entre os quilômetros 182 ao 100, em um trecho de 10,83 quilômetros. A autorização foi concedida à Eco-050 e e integra o corredor rodoviário que passa por Uberaba.

Como funciona o radar de velocidade média

Como funciona o radar de velocidade média — Foto: arte/g1

Imagine um motorista entrando em um trecho monitorado. O primeiro equipamento registra a passagem do veículo. Mais adiante, outro ponto de monitoramento identifica quando ele deixou o trecho.

O sistema cruza a distância entre os dois pontos com o tempo levado pelo veículo para percorrê-la. Assim, chega à velocidade média desenvolvida naquele segmento.

A lógica é diferente da dos radares convencionais, que verificam a velocidade instantânea do veículo em um determinado ponto.

Na prática, portanto, não basta reduzir a velocidade apenas diante de um equipamento e depois voltar a acelerar. O projeto pretende justamente avaliar o comportamento dos motoristas durante todo o trecho monitorado.

Os locais deverão ser sinalizados para informar os usuários sobre a realização do experimento.

Os condutores que passarem pelos trechos não serão multados pela velocidade média registrada durante o projeto-piloto.

A própria ANTT determinou que os testes terão caráter exclusivamente técnico, educativo e experimental. Nesta etapa, não será permitida a aplicação de autuações ou penalidades aos motoristas com fundamento exclusivamente na velocidade média calculada pelo sistema.

Isso não significa, porém, que os demais mecanismos de fiscalização de trânsito deixem de existir. A proibição prevista nas decisões se refere especificamente a penalidades baseadas exclusivamente na velocidade média registrada durante o experimento.

Uma eventual utilização futura da tecnologia para fiscalização com aplicação de multas dependerá de novas avaliações e das autorizações necessárias.

Durante os testes, as concessionárias deverão enviar mensalmente os resultados à ANTT. A agência vai analisar, entre outros pontos, a confiabilidade dos dados, o funcionamento dos equipamentos, o comportamento dos motoristas e o desempenho operacional do sistema.

A ideia é verificar como a tecnologia funciona em condições reais de uma rodovia antes de uma eventual adoção para outras finalidades.

articles.title: Após expulsão de turnê de Ed Sheeran, Macklemore doará US$ 1 milhão para ONGs pró-Palestina | G1
articles.standfirst: Macklemore era convidado de abertura da turnê 'Loop' pelos EUA e foi expulso após gritar 'Free Palestine' (Palestina Livre, em tradução literal) em show em Nova York.
articles.summary: Macklemore era convidado de abertura da turnê 'Loop' pelos EUA e foi expulso após gritar 'Free Palestine' (Palestina Livre, em tradução literal) em show em Nova York.
articles.body:
O rapper Macklemore anunciou nesta quarta-feira (16) que vai doar todo seu salário como integrante da turnê de Ed Sheeran para organizações que auxiliam o povo palestino. O valor anunciado pelo artista foi de US$ 1 milhão (R$ 5,1 milhões, na cotação atual) .

Macklemore era convidado de abertura da turnê "Loop" pelos EUA. No início de setembro, o rapper americano se apresentava no MetLife Stadium, em Nova Jersey (EUA), e gritou "Free Palestine" (Palestina Livre, em tradução literal).

Após pressão, a produtora do espetáculo retirou o cantor das apresentações seguintes .

Em comunicado no Instagram, Macklemore afirmou que o valor será enviado para seis organizações pró-Palestina.

O rapper também convidou o empresário Robert Kraft a fazer uma doação. Kraft, que é responsável pelo Gillet Stadium, em Boston, local de um dos shows da turnê, pressionou Ed Sheeran a retirar Macklemore da apresentação de abertura no local .

"Uma vida palestina não tem menos valor do que qualquer vida desta Terra. Sempre foi sobre isso. Não é sobe mim. Não é sobre a turnê. Não é sobre as manchetes ou controvérsias. É sobre o direito dos palestinos a liberdade, dignidade e segurança na sua própria terra natal", escreveu o rapper no Instagram.

Tudo começou no dia 4 de setembro. Segundo o jornal "The Guardian", o rapper americano, que fazia o show de abertura no MetLife Stadium, em Nova Jersey (EUA), gritou "Free Palestine" (Palestina Livre, em tradução literal) . Ele também afirmou que queria que as pessoas em Gaza e na Cisjordânia soubessem que não haviam sido esquecidas.

A declaração motivou uma petição do Conselho Israelense-Americano (Israeli American Council) pedindo a exclusão do rapper da turnê .

A Messina Touring Group, promotora responsável pela etapa dos Estados Unidos da turnê de Sheeran, informou à revista "Rolling Stone" que Macklemore não faria os shows das datas restantes.

"Como promotora da turnê 'Loop' de Ed Sheeran nos Estados Unidos, fomos informados pelos locais que sediarão as próximas datas da turnê de que eles não permitirão a realização dos shows com Macklemore no line-up. Isso resultaria no cancelamento da turnê e impactaria centenas de milhares de fãs. Após discussões com as partes envolvidas, Macklemore não se apresentará nas datas restantes como atração de apoio."

O rapper estava escalado para abrir oito dos dez shows restantes da turnê pelos EUA, com retomada prevista para 19 de setembro na Filadélfia. As cidades com locais de apresentação que teriam se oposto ao retorno de Macklemore incluem Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte, Indianápolis, Dallas e Tampa.

Macklemore canta durante show no Lollapalooza 2019 — Foto: Fábio Tito/G1

O cantor divulgou um longo comunicado na segunda-feira (14) sobre sua saída da turnê.

"Antes de começar, quero dizer algo que deveria ser óbvio. Neste momento, acho que isso importa. Eu não sou uma vítima", escreveu Macklemore no Instagram.

"Temos carreiras, dinheiro, oportunidades, segurança e público no mundo todo. Quaisquer que sejam as consequências que enfrentemos pelo que dizemos, podemos voltar para casa e para nossas famílias. As vítimas são os palestinos."

Já Ed Sheeran afirmou que a decisão partiu da promotora da turnê, a Messina Touring Group.

"Não sou cúmplice. Tenho minhas visões pessoais sobre esse conflito devastador. Só porque eu escolho não falar publicamente, não significa que eu não as tenho, e não significa que eu não me importe", publicou Sheeran.

Um comitê de investigação contratado pela Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) apontou em junho que Israel alvejou crianças deliberadamente na Faixa de Gaza. Segundo a comissão, tais práticas em Gaza configuram genocídio, crimes contra a humanidade e crimes de guerra.

O relatório da comissão da ONU afirmou ainda que cerca de 30% dos 73 mil mortos na guerra em Gaza eram crianças, pouco mais de 20 mil em números absolutos.

Ed Sheeran se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2024 — Foto: Leo Franco/AgNews

Os cantores Finneas, Aaron Rowe e Lukas Graham e a banda Beoga declararam nesta terça-feira (15) que não vão mais abrir os shows de Ed Sheeran.

Com isso, Sheeran perdeu todos os artistas de abertura de sua série de concertos, que tem datas previstas até 11 de dezembro.

Finneas, aliás, abriria as apresentações do cantor britânico em São Paulo nos dias 5 e 6 de dezembro. O grupo Beoga, além de abrir shows, também se apresentava ao lado de Sheeran em trechos de repertório influenciados pela música tradicional irlandesa.

Junto à decisão de cancelamento, os três cantores e o grupo manifestaram apoio à causa palestina.

"Artistas não devem ser silenciados por se manifestar contra a opressão", escreveu Finneas no Instagram.

"Deveríamos poder falar sobre guerra, sobre civis sendo mortos, sobre crianças que merecem crescer. Onde quer que vivam. Qualquer que seja a sua bandeira", afirmou Graham.

"Como irlandeses, conhecemos bem até demais genocídio, fome forçada e ocupação violenta", disse Rowe.

"Somos irlandeses que entendem colonialismo. Como membros fundadores do movimento Artistas Irlandeses pela Palestina, somos ativistas com compromisso pela justiça e continuaremos a ser", publicou a banda Beoga.

Sheeran ainda não comentou a saída dos demais artistas da turnê.

articles.title: When Trump gave Mark Carney White House key with a warning: 'Maybe they'll shoot you'
articles.summary: US News: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has revealed an unusual gift he received from US President Donald Trump in 2015 -- a large gold key that Trump tol.
articles.body: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has revealed an unusual gift he received from US President Donald Trump in 2015 -- a large gold key that Trump told him could be used to enter the White House. But there was a catch, delivered with a joke: “Maybe they’ll shoot you.”Carney recounted the exchange on Tuesday while speaking at the Canada Investment Summit in Toronto. He said the gift was presented to him when he met Trump at the White House in May 2025.According to Carney, Trump handed him a box containing what he described as a “big gold key” and told him it was a key to the White House.“You just bring it, they’ll let you in,” Carney recalled Trump telling him. Trump then added: “Maybe they’ll shoot you.”The remark drew laughter from the audience. Carney said the exchange captured something about the complicated relationship between the two neighbouring countries.“That sort of sums up the relationship that we have,” he said, later adding that he was only joking about the possibility of being shot.Carney also described the gift as a generous gesture, addressing Trump directly during the event. “Donald, if you’re listening, I am very grateful. It’s a very good gesture. He’s a very good host,” he said.The Canadian prime minister then contrasted the joke with the way visitors would be treated in Canada.“If you’re given a key to Canada, we’re going to welcome you,” Carney said.The anecdote comes at a particularly tense time in US-Canada relations. Washington and Ottawa are engaged in a trade dispute, with negotiations having broken down and the US imposing additional restrictions on some Canadian products. Canada has also been seeking to diversify its economic relationships and reduce its dependence on the US.Carney used the Toronto summit to pitch Canada as a destination for international investment, telling global investors that the country could emerge from the trade conflict with the US as a stronger and more independent economy. He is also pursuing closer economic and strategic ties with Europe as Canada looks to broaden its international partnerships.Ceremonial keys to the White HouseTrump has been giving ceremonial keys to the White House for year, including during his previous term. He told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu the same thing he told Carney: The key was essentially good forever.“Even when I’m not president anymore, you can walk up to the front gate of the White House and present it, and they will let you in,” he told Netanyahu, according to a 2022 book by Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law. Trump even gifted White House keys to visitors when he wasn’t president, including former Japanese Prime Minister Taro Aso, during a 2024 meeting at Trump Tower in New York.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Praadhyumn Indaana, the 17-year-old Montvale, New Jersey student whose AI model cut nuclear reactor heat-limit prediction error from about 63% to 5.5%; he won $50,000
articles.summary: US News: A better understanding of how much heat a nuclear reactor can safely handle could have implications far beyond a single engineering calculation. For 1.
articles.body: A better understanding of how much heat a nuclear reactor can safely handle could have implications far beyond a single engineering calculation. For 17-year-old Praadhyumn Indaana of Montvale, New Jersey, that challenge became the focus of an eight-month research project combining physics and artificial intelligence. According to the Davidson Institute, which named Indaana a 2026 Davidson Fellow, his physics-guided neural network reduced the average prediction error for critical heat flux from about 63% with conventional formulas to 5.5%. The work earned him a $50,000 Davidson Fellows Scholarship and recognition for a project aimed at improving predictions of an important nuclear-reactor operating limit.Why heat matters inside a nuclear reactorIn a nuclear reactor, water plays a critical role in removing heat from fuel rods. As the water boils against the fuel rods, it carries heat away. But there is a point at which the boiling process can no longer remove heat effectively. This threshold is known as critical heat flux, or CHF. Going beyond this limit can cause the cooling process to deteriorate rapidly. Steam can displace liquid water from the surface of the fuel rod, reducing cooling and causing the rod temperature to rise sharply. Because of the potential safety consequences, reactor operators and engineers need reliable ways to predict where this limit occurs.The difficulty, Indaana explains in his Davidson Institute project, is that conventional equations have generally been developed and tuned around particular experimental conditions. Their accuracy can therefore decline when they are applied outside those conditions.Building an AI model with physics built inIndaana approached the problem using a physics-regularized neural network. Instead of allowing an artificial-intelligence model to learn patterns from experimental data alone, he incorporated constraints based on physical theory. The model was trained using data from more than 10,000 real experiments. Indaana also incorporated bounds derived from hydrodynamic instability theory, helping prevent the model from producing predictions that violate known physical limits.This distinction was important because a conventional machine-learning model can struggle when it encounters situations for which there is little training data. According to Indaana, early versions of his models performed well in regions with large amounts of data but could produce physically unreasonable predictions when extrapolating into less represented high-quality-flow regions. He addressed the problem by adjusting the physics-based regularisation according to how closely different empirical correlations agreed for individual samples. He also added a penalty when predictions exceeded a known physical upper bound.Error falls from about 63% to 5.5%The resulting model produced a major improvement in prediction accuracy. According to the Davidson Institute, the conventional formulas showed average errors of about 63%, while Indaana's model reduced that figure to 5.5%. On a fixed testing dataset, the model achieved an R² value of 0.986, a statistical measure indicating how closely the model's predictions matched the observed data in that evaluation. Indaana compared its performance with widely used correlations, which he says produced errors an order of magnitude larger.The achievement does not mean that nuclear reactors can simply be operated closer to the heat limit. Reactor safety requirements remain stringent. Instead, more accurate prediction could help engineers understand the boundary more precisely and potentially reduce some of the conservatism built into reactor design and operation.An idea that began with a question about fusionThe project originated during a class on fusion energy that Indaana took through the Columbia University Science Honors Program. He asked why reactors that are already well characterised still need to operate conservatively. The answer led him to critical heat flux and the uncertainty surrounding its prediction across different operating regimes. He subsequently decided to investigate whether machine learning could improve the situation while remaining constrained by established physical knowledge.His interests extend beyond conventional nuclear reactors. Indaana told the Davidson Institute that he is interested in the intersection of materials science, quantum physics, computing and nuclear fusion, and hopes to study physics in college. His project also explores how physics-informed machine learning can be applied to engineering problems where knowledge is often expressed through empirical correlations and physical bounds rather than complete governing equations.An independent research effortIndaana completed the project over roughly eight months, working through literature review, data collection, feature engineering, model development, statistical evaluation and paper writing. He taught himself much of the thermohydraulics, physics-informed machine learning and statistics required for the work.He also used statistical methods including bootstrap resampling and paired nonparametric tests rather than relying solely on a reduction in prediction error. The model development and experiments were carried out on his own computer, with cloud resources such as Kaggle used for training. He received guidance from a mentor on the broader research process.Recognition with a $50,000 scholarshipIndaana's work earned him a place among the 2026 Davidson Fellows, a programme recognising students aged 18 and younger for significant achievements in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, literature and music. The Davidson Institute awarded him a $50,000 scholarship for his project.His research illustrates how artificial intelligence can be used not simply to process large amounts of data, but to combine data-driven learning with established scientific principles. In Indaana's case, that approach produced a substantially more accurate way of predicting a difficult engineering boundary, potentially offering a new way to approach problems where safety depends on understanding the limits of physical systems.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nigerian woman in Massachusetts charged after alleged illegal voting in federal elections
articles.summary: Gladys Adaeze Okafor allegedly falsified her citizenship on United States voter registration cards in Massachusetts to illegally cast ballots.
articles.body: A Nigerian woman living in the United States as a permanent resident in Massachusetts illegally voted in at least two elections after lying about her citizenship, authorities said. Gladys Adaeze Okafor, 56, has been charged by the Justice Department with unlawfully voting as an alien for allegedly casting ballots in the 2024 presidential primary election and the 2022 midterm elections despite not being a U.S. citizen. She is expected to appear in a Boston federal courtroom on Wednesday. CANADIAN NONCITIZEN ACCUSED OF ILLEGALLY VOTING IN FEDERAL AND STATE ELECTIONS Okafor repeatedly falsified her citizenship status on official documents under penalty of perjury to gain access to the ballot, federal prosecutors allege. In July 2022, she submitted a voter registration card and signed her name certifying that she was a U.S. citizen, authorities said. The City of Lynn subsequently registered her to vote. NONCITIZEN CHARGED WITH VOTING IN MINNESOTA 2024 ELECTION AFTER ADMITTING ‘MISTAKE’ TO INVESTIGATORS In October 2023, Okafor submitted another voter registration card where she checked a box saying she was an American citizen, prosecutors said. She then voted in the 2024 presidential primary election, court documents state. Okafor was born in Nigeria and obtained lawful permanent resident status in December 2022. However, she is not a U.S. citizen and has not applied for U.S. citizenship, prosecutors said. She faces up to a year in prison and up to $10,000 in fines. Recently, seven noncitizens were indicted in connection with an election integrity investigation in Texas. Earlier this month, the DOJ charged five people in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Wisconsin in cases involving alleged illegal voting or fraudulent registration during the 2022 or 2024 elections.

articles.title: Colbert confesses he's healthier away from late night, compares hosting to drinking a 'cup of poison'
articles.summary: Stephen Colbert agreed with Jimmy Kimmel Tuesday that he seemed happier and healthier in his post-late-night career, comparing hosting to drinking a cup of poison.
articles.body: Former "Late Show" host Stephen Colbert said Tuesday he doesn't drink a "cup of poison" every day after late-night host Jimmy Kimmel told him he looked happier and healthier away from late-night television. Colbert's final episode of "The Late Show" aired in May after CBS announced in 2025 it would be canceling the program. "Do you think about it ever?" Kimmel asked the former late-night host in an interview on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" "Nope," Colber said. "I have an opportunity to not think about the news every day, and I took it." JIMMY KIMMEL SAYS HE FELT 'DEFEATED' AFTER COLBERT SHOW WAS CANCELED, SAYS CBS IS USING 'MADE-UP NUMBERS' TUNING OUT: WHY MANY AMERICANS ARE SICK OF THE NEWS – ESPECIALLY TRUMP NEWS Kimmel told Colbert that the ex-late-night host seemed like a different person when he saw him at the Emmys. "When I saw you last night, I felt like you, I don’t know, you just seemed like a different person. You seemed happier, you seemed healthier," Kimmel said. Colbert quipped, "Like I don’t drink a cup of poison every day?" "The old gig, as I remember, was that, to be lowered like carbon rods into a radioactive pool every day. And then to be pulled out and put in front of a camera. And to radiate it back at the audience at a non-lethal rad level," Colbert said. JON STEWART ASKS WHETHER 'THE DAILY SHOW' IS LIKE HIGH-SUGAR FOOD GIVING US 'POLITICAL DIABETES' "Oh, the irony that someone from the left charged with spewing daily, anti-Trump missives feels happier that he's not engaged in grand delusions. It's almost as if having a life and hobbies outside of hating Trump and half the country is better for the soul. I, for one, am glad that Stephen appears to be getting the help he needs," Newsbusters managing editor Curtis Huock told Fox News Digital in a statement about the Kimmel-Colbert exchange. "This should be a lesson to the rest of the country: Never let politics completely consume your life. It sure seems as though Colbert actually touched grass and likes what he felt." Colbert's former program won Outstanding Variety Series at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards Monday, months after "The Late Show" aired its final episode in May. When asked after the ceremony about free speech and the future of late-night television, Colbert said he remained optimistic about the medium. RICKY GERVAIS REJECTS CALLS TO TONE DOWN COMEDY: 'BE OFFENDED IF YOU WANT' "If you can’t say something because you go to jail, that is a violation of free speech," Colbert said. "I think that late night is just as funny and just as vital as it ever has been, and I love watching Jimmy and Jimmy and John and John and Seth and everybody else. And I think I hope it goes on for a long time because you get to work with people like this, and that’s the greatest gift." When CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister asked Colbert directly whether he believed his show had been canceled because of Trump, the comedian appeared to repeatedly deflect rather than answer the question. Variety reported that the exchange came during a post-Emmys interview with Wagmeister and Variety co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "What ... Gayle, that’s a beautiful dress," Colbert said. After the reporter repeated the question, Colbert continued the bit. "Oh, I’m sorry, I’m deaf on this ear. What did you ... what did you say?" Colbert said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP When they again attempted to ask whether Trump was responsible for the cancellation, Colbert deflected once more. "You wanted to know who the most important member of my staff was? It’s me," Colbert said.

articles.title: When is it simply too cold to run outside safely? Here’s what running experts want you to know
articles.summary: Running experts give tips on how to stay warm while running in cold temperatures and suggest gear that will help you stay comfortable and warm.
articles.body: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends on our timelines, like whether honey is good for your skin. Frigid temperatures, icy roads and darker mornings can make running in the cold weather feel a lot more challenging. But running outside during any time of year has its benefits. The fresh air is nice, and the scenery is more engaging than being on a treadmill at the gym. “Running in the cold can be invigorating,” says Jay Silva, a Road Runners Club of America certified running coach with TeachMe.To, a site that helps you find coaches. “You just have to be smart about it and be prepared.” So, how can you prepare yourself to run in cold weather so you can still enjoy the benefits of exercising outside? The key is to take a few preventative steps to keep yourself safe and ensure you have the right gear. With that in mind, I consulted running experts to get all the intel you need for running in the cold and also how to know when it’s just too cold to go for a run. How to stay safe while running in the cold Running in cold weather can be safe — up to a certain point. Experts I spoke to agreed that running outdoors when it’s lower than 15 degrees Fahrenheit or the windchill is below 10 degrees Fahrenheit is not advised. If you take the right precautions, anything above those temperatures can be safe to run in. Here’s what they suggest to prepare: Spend time stretching: “It’s crucial to warm up indoors to get your muscles activated and ready,” says Taylor Wilson, a certified personal trainer in California. “Cold muscles are more prone to strain, so stretching can reduce risk of injury.” He suggests dynamic stretches like leg swings or lunges. Stay hydrated: When it’s hot and you’re sweating, it’s easy to remember to drink water. But staying hydrated is just as important in the colder weather. “Even though you sweat less, dehydration can creep up without you noticing it,” says Andrew White, a certified personal trainer and founder of Garage Gym Pro, a site that helps people set up home gyms. “Be mindful of drinking water before and after you run.” Watch for black ice: Black ice tends to pop up during the winter months. Pair that with the fact that the sun rises later and sets earlier and it can be easy to miss slippery patches on the road. “I can’t count the number of times I’ve been caught off guard by hidden ice patches, especially early in the morning,” says Silva. “Adjust your stride to be shorter and quicker to maintain better balance and avoid slipping.”Dress appropriately: Figuring out what to wear when running in cold weather can be tricky. While it’s tempting to bundle up so you’re warm as soon as you step outside, that may be the wrong move. You want to dress as if it is 10 to 20 degrees warmer than it actually is outside — you may be slightly cold when you first get outside, but you’ll warm up fast, says Silva. The other thing to consider is covering your hands, feet and head properly — three areas that tend to get particularly cold. Below, I’ve outlined exactly how to dress for running in colder weather and rounded up the best gear for it. The best cold weather running gear Using advice from the experts, I rounded up a list of cold running gear. All items below are recommended by experts or are highly rated and meet the requirements they said to look for. Feetures makes some of our favorite no-show socks and this version is made from merino wool, which is particularly good for the winter months. “Wool, or wool-blend socks, keep your feet warm even if they get a little damp,” says Silva. These unisex socks have a seamless toe construction to prevent irritation and cushioning on the bottom for comfort, according to the brand. NBC Selected editorial director, Lauren Swanson, has run multiple marathons and loves this thermal layer for winter training and beyond. “When I wear this shirt, I am rarely cold,” says Swanson. “Running in it feels cozy, but I’ll also wear it on particularly cold NYC mornings.” It’s made of polyester and spandex, so the fabric has a nice stretch to it, too, which is great for layering. These sneakers made our list of the best trail shoes thanks to their water-resistant and comfortable cushioned soles and deep lugs. Even if you aren’t technically hitting the trails, they can be a good option for cold-weather running. “If you’re running in snow or slushy conditions, trail shoes with extra grip or shoes with a water-resistant upper make a huge difference,” says Silva. These shoes are available in men’s and women’s sizes. NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin, who runs regularly, says that these tights never get itchy or slip. They have pockets for convenient storage and a wide waistband with an internal drawstring for a customized fit that keeps them in place as you move, according to the brand. They’re also sweat-resistant and are thin enough to be layered under sweats or other pants for added warmth on really frigid days. This running jacket is available in versions for men and women and is from NBC Selected editor-favorite brand On. The lightweight jacket is made from wind- and water-resistant material and has hidden airflow vents to prevent sweating. Because it is so lightweight, it is a good jacket to wear over other layers. It also folds up small into its own pocket, so you can easily pack it for runs while you’re traveling. This adjustable belt has pockets for your phone, keys, credit cards and two 10-ounce water bottles, which will help remind you to stay hydrated on colder runs. The belt is lined with silica gel to minimize chafing and bouncing while you jog, and the outer portion has reflectors to keep you visible in the early morning or during the evening. These gloves are lightweight and made from a fabric blend that is specifically meant to help you regulate your temperature, according to the brand. The fabric also has stretch to provide a snug fit and is touchscreen compatible, so you don’t need to take them off if you want to change the song on your phone or answer a text. Solve two common cold weather running problems with this hat. It will cover your ears to keep them warm when it’s cold out and it has a built-in light to make you more visible to cars when it’s dark outside. The LED light has three brightness levels, has eight hours of runtime and is rechargeable. The hat comes in more than 40 colors, making it easy to find one that suits your style. How to dress for running in cold weather Dressing to run in low temperatures goes beyond just picking the right pieces like the ones above — how you utilize them matters, too. Our experts shared exactly how to get dressed to stay warm when you head outside for a run during the colder months. Learn to layer “When you first step outside, you should feel a bit cold,” says Silva. “If you feel cozy right away, you’ve probably overdressed and will be uncomfortable once your body heats up.” Layering is the smartest thing you can do to prevent this — not only can it keep you cozy, but it allows you to peel layers off to prevent yourself from overheating if you start to get warm as you run. Here, the layers you should consider: Base layer: A moisture-wicking base layer — like a shirt or leggings made of merino wool or synthetic fabrics — will help keep sweat off your skin, preventing chill when you slow down or stop, says Silva. This layer should be relatively thin so you can layer on top of it without feeling bulky.Mid-layer: If it’s below freezing, adding a thermal shirt or fleece pullover on top of your base layer will add extra warmth.Outer layer: A wind- and water-resistant jacket like On’s Weather Jacket will help keep out the cold and keep the warmth you create close to your body. Select one that you can zip up or down as you move to stay warmer or cool down a bit, says Silva. Protect your hands, head and feet “Wind chill on your hands or ears can be brutal,” says Silva. A good hat or headband that can be pulled over your ears will help. Gloves that protect your fingers without making your hands sweat are also a good purchase. If you like to listen to music or carry your phone while running, consider touchscreen-friendly gloves, like the New Balance Performance Touchscreen Gloves. Regarding footwear, look for running sneakers with deeper treads — this will give you traction as you move over potentially icy terrain, says Wilson. We like the Hoka Mafate 5 Trail Running Sneakers for this. And be sure to pair your sneakers with the right kind of socks for cold weather. Moisture-wicking socks will help you prevent blisters and keep feet warm,” he adds. Go for gear that keeps you visible During the colder months, running in low-light conditions is more common because the sun tends to rise later and set earlier. “Reflective gear will help you stay visible to cars and cyclists,” says White. Look for running clothes with reflective details or consider getting a reflective vest or headlamp or something like the Melasa Beanie Hat with Light, which makes it easier for others to spot you as you run. Taking these extra precautions can help keep you safe. articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com. Somehow, we've made it to our third Hump Day of September. Lordy. Time flies when it's football season! This is also our final Hump Day before the official beginning of Fall. That's right. Technically, it starts next Tuesday — astronomically speaking. Just to give folks outside of Florida an idea of where things stand down here at the moment, we're all currently looking forward to Friday, because the Dew points around the state are supposed to drop 10 degrees. Not the actual temps themselves, of course. The dew points. That's basically the humidity level. So, it's still going to be unbearably hot, but at least it'll be slightly less humid for a few hours in the morning! Break out the firewood. articles.title: Renaming Lake Erie? US City Council passes satirical resolution to name it 'Gulf of Cleaveland', says it's 'shockingly dumb' but why should Trump have all the fun
articles.summary: US News: Inspired by President Donald Trump renaming Lake Ontario and Lake America, a city council has even passed the resolution to rename Lake Erie as the \"G.
articles.body: Inspired by President Donald Trump renaming Lake Ontario and Lake America, a city council has even passed the resolution to rename Lake Erie as the "Gulf of Cleaveland". There was simmering tension over Lake Erie as Pennsylvania state Rep David Maloney proposed renaming Lake Erie as "Lake Pennsylvania" arguing that Pennsylvania has a special claim because it is the state's only Great Lake.Cleaveland council passed the motion in a 13-1 vote after Council member Kris Harsh brought an emergency resolution that is not legally binding. So, the name is not getting changed but no one is taking a backseat when it comes to the renaming spree. Harsh said to Newsweek that he was aware that calling Lake Erie "Gulf of Cleaveland" is shockingly dumb that that's the point. "If everybody gets to rename something, then screw it. We'll make it the Gulf of Cleveland," he said clarifying that he introduced the measure as a satiric response."It's a convenient distraction for [Trump] to cover up the fact that he started a war that he can't win but we're all losing… Americans need to stop thinking that this is all a joke and start to realize that this is real and I know the constant daily circus distracts people from that reality but that's what I was trying to cut through. I know the Gulf of Cleveland is a stupid idea. I'm fully aware of that," he said."President Trump's orders to assign new names without reference to history, tradition, and other acts of Congress have opened the door for United States officials to rename other geography," Harsh said. "Thanks to him, this is a man who clearly isn't afraid to say what no one is thinking.""Keep in mind, there's a very real person in Pennsylvania right now who wants to rename it the Lake of Pennsylvania," Harsh said. "We cannot, as Ohioans, let the Pennsylvanians get a jump on us. It's our lake."“I can hear them now, saying, ‘Kris, it’s not even a gulf; it’s a lake,’” Harsh said while presenting the proposal. His response: “Who cares?”The council's satiric resolution even directs Cleveland departments to use “Gulf of Cleveland” in city-generated maps and documents. It also says the city will contact major mapping companies, including Apple and Google, asking them to reflect the new name.“Sometimes when things get so absurd, you just kind of got to poke a little fun at how ridiculous they’ve got,” he said after the vote. He added that the measure took about 15 minutes and cost the city nothing.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield loses bet to coach Todd Bowles, has 'rough couple of days' including at press conference
articles.summary: Baker Mayfield lost a friendly bet to Todd Bowles over the Michigan-Oklahoma game, but a revenge matchup against the Cleveland Browns looms Sunday.
articles.body: It's not all super serious for Baker Mayfield as he begins preparation for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns. There's actually kind of a surprisingly jovial atmosphere around the Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback and his team. Mayfield, you see, stepped to the microphone on Wednesday to begin his weekly press conference wearing a University of Michigan basketball tank top. An ill-fitting one at that. MICHIGAN EXERCISES CLOCK DEMONS FROM WEEK ONE WIN, VANQUISHES 11TH RANKED OKLAHOMA IN ANN ARBOR Head coach Todd Bowles initially stood in the doorway humming the University of Michigan fight song and shouting, "Let's go blue!" "That hurts, that hurts real bad," Mayfield said. "It's been a rough couple of days." And why would Mayfield be wearing a child-size Michigan tank top? "Oklahoma versus Michigan," he explained. "Todd's son was on the winning side of it. The Sooners were not. And so, therefore, I squeezed into this little tank top." Bowles' son, Troy, plays for the Wolverines. Mayfield played for Oklahoma. So there was some bragging rights involved that led to a friendly wager about the Saturday matchup. But then ... Michigan 17. Oklahoma 10. So, quite a funny moment considering the expression on Mayfield's face. But that moment could be understood to be perhaps more meaningful in that it speaks to the mindset for the Buccaneers' quarterback, his coach, and perhaps the team. The Bucs are 0-1 headed to Sunday's game against the Browns. And Mayfield in the season-opener struggled in a 33-27 season-opening loss against the Cincinnati Bengals because he didn't throw a touchdown pass but lost three fumbles, including one around the goal line when it seemed the Bucs would be scoring. So, actually, that hurts. It hurts Bowles, who is under some expectation to get his team into the postseason. And it hurts Mayfield, who just last week agreed to a three-year contract extension worth a whopping $165 million and putting him among the league's highest-paid quarterbacks. Neither Bowles nor Mayfield met expectation in the regular-season opener. So this week the script needs to flip against the Browns. DESHAUN WATSON REMAINS THE CLEVELAND BROWNS STARTING QUARTERBACK BUT THAT COMES WITH AN EXPIRATION DATE There's more. Did we mention happy-bet-loser Mayfield played for the Browns from 2018, when he was the NFL's No. 1 overall draft pick, through the 2021 season? Mayfield wasn't such a happy loser when the Browns shipped him to Carolina after deciding Deshaun Watson would be a better fit. Mayfield was actually quite angry at the time. And Sunday is obviously a pressure-packed opportunity to get some measure of revenge. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Mayfield better get his retribution while he can in that opportunity. Because he won't be getting it from another friendly Michigan versus Oklahoma wager anytime soon. articles.title: Alex Ovechkin, all-time NHL goal scorer, appears in ad supporting Vladimir Putin
articles.summary: Washington Capitals forward and NHL all-time leading goal scorer Alex Ovechkin appeared in an ad backing Russian President Vladimir Putin.
articles.body: Washington Capitals forward and NHL all-time leading goal scorer Alex Ovechkin appeared in an ad backing Russian President Vladimir Putin, bringing renewed attention to the player’s controversial, longtime support for the authoritarian ruler. The TV spot came to light just this week, showing Ovechkin standing in a group that included Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and retired Detroit Red Wings defenseman Viacheslav “Slava” Fetisov, professing their support of Putin’s United Russia party. The Capitals confirmed that Ovechkin appeared in the spot and said the player’s off-the-ice political work will have no impact on the upcoming NHL season. “Alex Ovechkin is a Russian citizen who lives in Moscow with his family during the offseason and will live there following his retirement,” team spokesman Sergey Kocharov said in a statement to NBC News on Wednesday. “This summer, while in Russia, he was asked by his country to participate in a video campaign. As the longest-tenured athlete in Washington, D.C. and a pillar of the community, his focus and ours is on the season ahead and the continued impact he makes on the ice and in our city.” Ovechkin has had a long, close relationship with Putin. Back in 2017, Ovechkin launched the “Putin Team” social movement. Russia has been an international pariah since Putin — who has run the country as president or prime minister since 2000 — launched the invasion of neighboring Ukraine in February 2022. Over 250,000 Russian soldiers, up to 100,000 Ukrainian soldiers and nearly 14,000 Ukrainian civilians are estimated to have been killed in the war. Hall of Fame goaltender Dominik ‘The Dominator” Hašek has been particularly outspoken against the Putin regime and its supporters. Hašek called Russia’s ongoing invasion “an imperialist war in Ukraine” and circled Ovechkin’s face in a picture of campaign supporters in an X posting this week. “Because of each of them, many Ukrainians and Russians will be killed,” wrote Hašek, a native of Pardubice, Czech Republic, who played 16 seasons in the NHL, 9 with the Buffalo Sabres. Ovechkin, who turns 41 this week, has tallied 929 goals in 21 NHL seasons, all with the Caps. The three-time Hart Trophy winner overtook Wayne Gretzky on the all-time goal scoring list when he found the back of the net during an April 6, 2025 game against the New York Islanders. Ovechkin has hoisted the Stanley Cup once, leading Washington to the title in 2018. He also won the Conn Smythe Trophy that year, as playoff MVP. The Caps open training camp on Thursday, ahead of the 2026-27 campaign. Washington’s regular season opener is set for Oct. 2 against the Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes.

articles.body: Americans traveling to Cambodia are facing a new warning from the U.S. State Department as officials flag security and safety risks across parts of the country. The department issued a Level 2 "Exercise Increased Caution" advisory for Cambodia on Sept. 15, citing crime, unrest and unexploded ordnance. Located in Southeast Asia, Cambodia shares borders with Thailand, Vietnam and Laos. DEADLY DRUGS, CRIME AND KIDNAPPING FLAGGED AT TOURIST HOT SPOT KNOWN FOR ANCIENT WONDERS While the country overall remains at Level 2, some areas carry the State Department's highest Level 4 warning, or "Do Not Travel." Americans are advised not to travel to areas along the Cambodian-Thai border due to unrest, according to the advisory. The State Department also warns travelers to exercise increased caution in Phnom Penh due to crime. The provinces of Battambang, Banteay Meanchey, Pursat, Siem Reap, Pailin, Preah Vihear and Kampong Thom all carry increased warnings due to unexploded ordnance, the advisory notes. The State Department also highly recommends purchasing travel insurance and checking whether coverage includes evacuation assistance, medical insurance and trip cancellations. Travelers are also warned about Cambodia's strict drug laws. Cambodia has a "zero-tolerance policy for drug offenses," according to State Department travel guidance, and possessing even small quantities of illegal drugs can lead to arrest and detention. articles.title: 7 missing women — 5 of whom are believed to be dead — connected to Philadelphia home, officials say
articles.summary: Seven women who disappeared over more than a decade have been linked to a Philadelphia house where investigators recovered more than 1 million images and videos, including footage that police say appears to show women unconscious, injured or dead.
articles.body: Seven women who disappeared over more than a decade have been linked to a Philadelphia house where investigators recovered more than 1 million images and videos, including footage that police say appears to show women unconscious, injured or dead. Five of the seven women are believed to be dead, although no bodies have been recovered, Philadelphia police said Wednesday. The expanding investigation centers on Raymond “R.C.” Horsch, a photographer of sexually explicit material who died in 2025 at 82, and the home he shared with his son. Deputy Police Commissioner Frank Vanore said investigators have identified 58 people depicted in material recovered from the house. Four appeared lifeless or unconscious, while 10 others later died of suspected drug overdoses at locations away from the property, he said. Police have located 41 other people seen in the material. Sixteen declined or were reluctant to be interviewed, while detectives were working to interview another 25, according to Vanore. Investigators have reviewed only about 30% of the digital evidence, leaving hundreds of thousands of images and videos to be examined. Authorities have not announced homicide charges in connection with any of the missing women. The case began with an apparently unrelated encounter in June, when a federal park ranger approached an illegally parked BMW near Philadelphia’s Independence Hall. Inside were Horsch’s 44-year-old son, Eugene Horsch, and a woman carrying identification belonging to Blaire Tonzelli, who had been missing since 2023, police said. The ranger also found two handguns, approximately $8,000 worth of illegal drugs and credentials identifying Eugene Horsch as a federal law enforcement officer, authorities said. The credentials, including one purporting to be from the Drug Enforcement Administration, were fraudulent, investigators said. The encounter led authorities to the Horsch home on West Chew Avenue in Philadelphia’s Olney neighborhood where searches uncovered firearms, fraudulent federal law-enforcement credentials, drugs, computer equipment, containers of unidentified substances and five urns holding cremated remains, investigators said. The city’s homicide detectives, agents from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and a bomb squad returned with another search warrant June 25. That search uncovered what appeared to be a home laboratory containing vessels filled with an unidentified oily substance, investigators said. Digital devices recovered from the property contained more than 1 million images and videos, many depicting women inside the house, police said. Who are the women tied to this property? Investigators have connected seven missing women to the house or the people who lived there, police said. Five are believed to be dead. Officials have not recovered the bodies of any of the women. Blair Tonzelli was 35 when she disappeared in 2023. Her identification was presented by the woman found with Eugene Horsch. Amy McHale disappeared in June 2016. She had previously been married to Raymond Horsch, and her family has said she was last seen at the house. Nicole Fusaro disappeared in 2018 at the age of 27. Investigators said footage recovered from the house appears to show her unconscious and injured. Maribel Fresses was 27 when she disappeared in 2018. Investigators said footage recovered from the house appears to show her unconscious and injured. Gabrielle Amarando was 22 when she disappeared in 2012. Police said she also appears unconscious and injured in the recovered footage. Authorities have not publicly identified the other two missing women or explained how each is connected to the property. Police said images and videos of Fresses and Amarando led detectives to conclude that the women were likely dead. Investigators have not found their remains or DNA inside the house, however. Video appears to show woman being strangled In another set of videos dated from 2017, Raymond Horsch appears nude with a woman inside the house, Vanore said. Horsch appeared to be operating the camera while another person recorded from a fixed position. During the videos, Vanore said that the woman appears to use narcotics before Horsch hands her money and then ties her to the bed using handcuffs and puts a ziptie around her neck. The woman appears to lose consciousness. Investigators have not determined whether she died or whether she is among the missing women connected to the property.

articles.title: An anonymous donor gave Cincinnati $1.8 million to restore 228 acres of forest; the 5-year project is the city's biggest park reforestation effort in nearly 100 years
articles.summary: US News: An anonymous donor has given Cincinnati $1.8 million to restore 228 acres of forest at French Park in Amberley Village. The five-year project is being.
articles.body: An anonymous donor has given Cincinnati $1.8 million to restore 228 acres of forest at French Park in Amberley Village. The five-year project is being described as the city’s largest reforestation effort in a park in nearly 100 years. According to WVXU, the restoration will focus on removing invasive plants, planting native trees, improving wildlife habitat and upgrading trails and access points. The donation will also fund a Natural Resource Specialist who will supervise the work throughout the project. French Park is spread across more than 280 acres and includes wooded hillsides, creeks, meadows, hiking trails and an event space. The Cincinnati Parks Foundation believes the effort could eventually become a model for restoring urban forests in other Cincinnati parks and beyond.A major restoration effort begins at French ParkCincinnati Parks has begun work on what it calls its largest reforestation effort in a city park in nearly a century. The project is centred on French Park, a large natural area whose forests have increasingly been affected by invasive plants.The $1.8 million donation will support restoration work over five years. Although the donor has chosen not to reveal their identity, the gift will have a public impact. Residents and visitors will be able to see the results as sections of the park are cleared, replanted and improved.The first phase of work is already underway. Crews are removing invasive species, including honeysuckle, privet and burning bush. These plants can spread quickly through woodland areas and prevent native trees, shrubs and wildflowers from receiving enough sunlight, water and space to grow.As the invasive growth is cleared, Cincinnati Parks plans to encourage the return of native vegetation and establish a new generation of trees.French Park’s natural landscapeFrench Park covers slightly more than 280 acres in Amberley Village. Its landscape includes hillsides, creeks, meadows and 228 acres of wooded forest.The park is also used regularly by people looking for outdoor recreation. Its hiking trails attract walkers and nature lovers, while a popular event space brings visitors for gatherings and community activities.The restoration project is intended to protect these existing uses while improving the condition of the forest. The aim is not simply to remove unwanted plants, but to create a healthier and more balanced landscape that can support wildlife and remain welcoming to visitors.A forest can appear thick and green while still being ecologically unhealthy. Invasive plants may fill the understory, but that does not necessarily mean they are providing the same benefits as native vegetation. When a small number of aggressive species dominate an area, they can reduce plant diversity and make it more difficult for young native trees to survive.Why invasive species are a concernHoneysuckle, privet and burning bush are among the invasive plants being removed from French Park. Once established, these species can form dense layers across the forest floor and crowd out native growth.That can affect the entire woodland ecosystem. Native plants provide food and shelter for local insects, birds and other animals. When they disappear, the wildlife that depends on them can also be affected.Dense invasive growth may also change the appearance and experience of a park. Visitors can find it difficult to see through the vegetation, follow natural sightlines or appreciate the structure of the forest. Cincinnati Parks Director Jason Barron said invasive species have made some parts of the woods so crowded that people can barely see the forest beyond them.Removing invasive plants is therefore an important first step, but it is not the end of the work. Restoration teams must also monitor cleared areas, protect new plantings and prevent invasive species from returning. That is one reason the five-year timeline and the dedicated specialist position are important to the project.Native trees and wildlife habitatThe restoration plan includes planting native trees and improving habitat for wildlife. Native species are adapted to the local environment and can provide resources that regional birds, insects and mammals recognise and use.New trees will also help maintain the forest over the long term. Older trees are valuable, but a healthy woodland needs different age groups, including young saplings, mature trees and older growth. Planting and protecting young trees can help ensure that the forest continues to exist for future generations.The work could also improve the relationship between the park’s natural areas and its trails. With careful planning, visitors may eventually experience a more varied landscape, including open sections, native understory, shaded woodland and clearer views near paths.The project’s benefits may not be immediate. Forest restoration often takes years, and some changes may be subtle at first. However, removing invasive plants and giving native vegetation room to recover can establish the foundation for a stronger ecosystem.A project with a wider purposeCincinnati Parks and the Cincinnati Parks Foundation see French Park as more than a single restoration site. They hope the project will produce a practical model that can be adapted in other city parks.That model could help officials decide how to assess forest health, prioritise invasive species removal, select native trees and manage restored areas over time. The experience gained at French Park may also show how large-scale conservation projects can be carried out in places that remain open and useful to the public.The Cincinnati Parks Foundation said the work has the potential to become a model for restoring urban forests throughout Cincinnati and beyond.Urban forest projects can be complicated because they must balance ecological needs with public access, safety and maintenance. A park is not a sealed-off nature reserve. People walk through it, hold events, use its trails and depend on it as an open space within the city.The French Park project is designed to address both sides of that challenge. It will focus on the health of the forest while also improving trails and access for visitors.Why urban forests matterCincinnati Mayor Aftab Pureval said natural places are among a community’s most valuable public assets. In a statement reported by WVXU, he described green spaces as important to quality of life, physical and mental well-being, and family time in nature.French Park offers those benefits in a setting close to the city. Its woods provide a place to walk, observe wildlife and take a break from busy urban surroundings. The creeks, meadows and hillsides add to the park’s character and create different habitats within the same landscape.The anonymous donation may also encourage wider public attention on the condition of city forests. Reforestation is often associated with planting large numbers of trees, but successful restoration involves much more. It requires removing competing plants, understanding local ecology, maintaining access and caring for new growth after planting.By funding a five-year programme and a specialist position, the gift gives Cincinnati Parks the time and resources needed for that broader approach.A long-term investment in the parkThe French Park restoration effort is being compared with the creation and reforestation of Mount Airy Forest in the 1930s. That historical connection highlights the scale of the current project.Nearly a century after Cincinnati undertook a major forest renewal effort at Mount Airy, the city is preparing to restore another large urban woodland. The two projects belong to different eras, but they share a similar goal: protecting natural areas so they can serve the public for decades.The work at French Park will unfold gradually over the next five years. Some areas may look different as invasive vegetation is removed, while other sections will change more slowly as native trees and plants become established.For residents, the most meaningful results may eventually be seen in simple ways. A clearer trail, a young native tree, more birds along a creek or a healthier forest floor can all signal that the woodland is recovering.The donor’s identity may remain unknown, but the purpose of the gift is clear. It will help Cincinnati restore one of its important natural spaces and develop a strategy for caring for urban forests in the future.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends on our timelines, like how often you should wash jeans. If you’ve ever lived in a studio apartment, a small house, or a place without laundry hookups, you’ve probably eyed a portable washer and dryer online at least once. They promise the convenience of in-unit laundry without the space (or plumbing) a full-size setup demands. But do these smaller appliances actually get your clothes clean? And what about the drain on your plumbing and electricity, not to mention the bills? I spoke with appliance experts to find out what portable washers and dryers can realistically do, where they fall short, and whether they’re worth the investment. Do portable washers and dryers really work? The short answer is yes — with some caveats. “Portable washers and dryers can be as effective as regular-sized ones, provided that you’re using them for smaller loads,” says Dennis Godynuk, an appliance technician and owner of Comfort Appliance Repair in Nashville, Tenn. In other words, if you’re washing everyday clothes in smaller quantities, you shouldn’t notice much of a difference in cleaning performance compared to a full-size machine. But where portable models can fall short is capacity and convenience. “They are essentially smaller versions of their regular-sized counterparts, which means they have smaller load capacity and may not be able to accommodate bulky items like blankets,” Godynuk explains. He also points out a common drawback with portable dryers specifically: “Some dryers may take a longer time to dry clothes because they lack vents.” That means bigger items like comforters or bulky winter coats may need a trip to the laundromat, and dry time for everyday loads could run longer than you’re used to. The best portable washing machines Ideal for apartments, dorms, tiny homes or RVs, this portable washer has a 26.5-pound capacity. It has a stainless steel tub, six wash-cycle settings, three water-level settings and a quick-connect sink adapter. Rolling wheels and side handles make it easy to move between rooms — so you could store it in a closet or other room between uses. This portable washer has a 17.8-pound capacity in a compact, a stainless steel drum and a built-in drain pump. It also comes equipped with five adjustable water levels, eight washing modes and a child safety lock. Shoppers say they like it because it runs quietly and gets clothes “very clean.” Compact and space-savvy, this Comfee portable washer is perfect for much smaller spaces. Despite its miniature footprint, it delivers full-automatic washing power for up to 7 pounds of clothing. A clear LED display makes selecting cycles and monitoring progress simple, adding convenience to its portable design. The best portable dryers This front-load tumble dryer has a stainless steel tub with a see-through door. It can be mounted on a wall or left standing. This is best for those who don’t have much to dry, as it can only hold up to 5.5-pounds of items at a time, which is about a third of what a full-size dryer holds. This dryer is quite large for a portable model and holds up to 9 pounds of clothing. It has four different drying modes — strong, intelligent, eco and normal. It also has a wide door and transparent window for convenience. This dryer has a 5.5-pound capacity with a stainless steel drum and front-loading design. It offers four programs: high temperature, sensor dry, air dry, and anti-wrinkle. It’s compact and apartment-friendly, but keep in mind that it requires a 4-inch venting duct, which you can buy separately for less than $10. How I picked the best portable washers and dryers I asked appliance experts what shoppers should keep in mind before buying a portable washer and dryer. Here’s what they said to consider: Capacity: Check the cubic footage of the drum before you buy, and think honestly about your typical load size. Portable machines generally hold less than half of what a full-size washer or dryer can, so if you frequently wash bulky items like comforters or blankets and will still need to take consistent trips to the laundromat, you should think long and hard about whether a portable is the right investment.Size: Measure your space carefully, including doorways and hallways the unit will need to pass through during delivery. Portable models are designed to fit tight spots like closets and apartments or be wheeled in and out of closets, but exact dimensions vary by brand and model, so don’t assume “portable” means it will fit anywhere.Brand: Stick with reputable manufacturers known for reliable portable appliances, and look into each brand’s track record for durability and customer service. Popular brands are often easier to find replacement parts for and qualified repair technicians down the line.Energy efficiency: Look for Energy Star-certified models, which use less water and electricity than standard machines. Since portable units are often used more frequently to compensate for smaller loads, efficiency can make a real difference in your utility bills over time. Who should buy portable appliances? Portable laundry appliances aren’t the right fit for everyone. “Large households should avoid these compact appliances,” says Godynuk. “The same goes for those who often wash bulky items.” In other words, if you’re regularly doing laundry for a family of four or more, or if your routine involves comforters, sleeping bags, or heavy blankets, a portable setup will likely leave you frustrated and running more loads than you’d like. On the other hand, portable washers and dryers can be a great solution for the right living situation. “They’re best suited for people living in apartments, smaller homes or other spaces where a full-size laundry setup won’t fit,” says Glenn Lewis, president of Mr. Appliance, an appliance repair franchise. “These designs can provide useful laundry capabilities without requiring as much room.” For singles, couples, or small households in space-constrained homes, that trade-off between capacity and convenience is often worth it. articles.title: No ‘Welcome to the United States’ guide for new Green Card recipients? USCIS says information available online
articles.summary: US News: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) appears to have stopped including its printed “Welcome to the United States: A Guide for New Immig.
articles.body: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) appears to have stopped including its printed “Welcome to the United States: A Guide for New Immigrants” with newly issued green cards, according to recent reports from Green Card recipients. The change has drawn attention because the booklet has traditionally served as an introductory guide for new lawful permanent residents, explaining their rights and responsibilities and providing information on settling in the US.USCIS has not announced that the guide has been formally discontinued but they said that all information was available online. The agency's website continues to make the guide available online, and its official page for new green card holders still lists the publication among the resources available to permanent residents.The reports about the missing booklet appear to be based on recent Green Card recipients who say their cards arrived without the printed guide. The development was reported by Newsweek based on claims on Reddit.What is the ‘Welcome to the United States’ guide?The publication is an official USCIS guide titled “Welcome to the United States: A Guide for New Immigrants.” It provides basic information intended to help new permanent residents settle in the country.The guide covers subjects including maintaining permanent resident status, working in the United States, paying taxes, travelling internationally, finding housing and healthcare, and understanding rights and responsibilities.USCIS continues to host the publication as a downloadable PDF on its website.The agency's “After We Grant Your Green Card” webpage also continues to direct permanent residents to the guide.The apparent removal of the printed booklet does not change the legal status of a person who has been granted permanent residence. USCIS continues to issue Permanent Resident Cards, commonly known as green cards, to lawful permanent residents.The booklet itself is informational. It is not a required immigration document, and not receiving a physical copy does not invalidate a green card or alter the holder's rights and obligations as a permanent resident.The guide remains available electronically, meaning new immigrants can still access the same USCIS information online.Why the change is drawing attentionThe development came at a time when the Trump administration has introduced a series of changes affecting the US immigration system, including changes to immigration processing and screening.That broader context has prompted speculation about whether the disappearance of the printed welcome guide represents another policy change.A former USCIS supervisor, Douglas S Pierce, told Newsweek that the agency might have stopped mailing the guide to cut printing, postage and storage costs by moving materials online.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
