articles.title: Arizona realtor Layne Lundeen, 67, who was duct-taped to his seat after American Airlines flight outburst, says he ‘doesn’t remember any of what happened’: ‘I assaulted a police officer?’
articles.summary: US News: An American Airlines passenger who was allegedly restrained with duct tape and zip ties after becoming unruly on a flight to Newark told a court he ha.
articles.body: An American Airlines passenger who was allegedly restrained with duct tape and zip ties after becoming unruly on a flight to Newark told a court he had no memory of the mid-air incident, one day after his arrest.Layne Lundeen, 67, appeared before a court in Annapolis, Maryland, where he reportedly expressed confusion about the allegations against him. According to The Banner, which obtained audio of the hearing, Lundeen said, “I don’t remember any of what happened.”When District Court Commissioner George Haag read the accusations, Lundeen reportedly asked, “I assaulted a police officer? Is that what it says?” He then added, “I don’t have my glasses.”Layne Lundeen says he didn’t know how he ended up in MarylandLundeen repeatedly told the commissioner that he could not recall the events surrounding the flight.“Oh my God. What a mess. I don’t remember any of it,” he reportedly said.Haag later asked him what had brought him to Maryland. Lundeen replied that he had been travelling to New York City and did not know how he had ended up in Maryland.“I came to New York City. I don’t know how I got to Maryland. I was supposed to land in New Jersey,” he said.The 67-year-old Arizona realtor had reportedly been travelling to help one of his daughters move into a new apartment. He also said it was her birthday.“I got a double whammy for my trip. Well, now it’s a triple whammy,” Lundeen reportedly told the commissioner.Flight diverted after alleged outburstAccording to police, witnesses said Lundeen “became increasingly unruly” during the American Airlines flight.The alleged behaviour was reportedly serious enough that fellow passengers restrained him using duct tape and zip ties. The aircraft was subsequently forced to make an emergency landing in Baltimore.Lundeen faces charges of second-degree assault and disorderly conduct.His seatmate, author and Messianic rabbi Jonathan Cahn, has also spoken about the alleged incident. Cahn said the two had initially been having a cordial conversation before their discussion turned towards spirituality.Cahn previously described Lundeen as appearing to change suddenly, claiming he went from being friendly to becoming enraged.Jonathan Cahn recalls alleged confrontationAccording to Cahn, their conversation touched on “the reality of the real power of god on Earth and in our lives,” after which Lundeen allegedly became angry.Cahn claimed Lundeen began cursing and making statements against Jesus and God, saying, “It’s all bulls–t. Jesus is bulls–t.”During his court appearance, Lundeen reportedly said the only thing he remembered was speaking with the man seated next to him.The episode also had professional consequences for Lundeen. The Arizona realtor was reportedly let go by Tucson-based Long Realty Company after footage and accounts of the incident went viral.Lundeen released ahead of October hearingLundeen was released on his own recognizance following the hearing, according to The Banner. He was ordered to abstain from alcohol and drugs, apart from prescribed medications.As the hearing ended, Lundeen asked Haag how far he was from New York City.“That depends on mode of transportation and traffic,” the commissioner replied, adding that it would be at least a few hours.Lundeen's next court appearance in the District Court of Maryland for Anne Arundel County in Glen Burnie is scheduled for October 19.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Macklemore pledges $1 million to Palestinian relief, challenges Robert Kraft to match it
articles.summary: Macklemore is donating $1 million of his earnings to Palestinian relief organizations following his removal from Ed Sheeran’s tour and he’s invited New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft to do the same.
articles.body: Macklemore is donating $1 million of his earnings to Palestinian relief organizations following his removal from Ed Sheeran’s tour and he’s invited New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft to do the same. In an Instagram post Wednesday, Macklemore said he wanted to “bring the conversation back where it belongs.” He specified that the money was the entirety of his net earnings from Sheeran’s tour, and that it would go to six organizations working to support Palestinians. “Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protection,” Macklemore wrote. “A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any life on this earth.” The statement comes just two days after Macklemore, whose real name is Ben Haggerty, announced he’d been dropped from Sheeran’s tour after venues threatened to cancel shows in response to Macklemore’s pro-Palestinian performance. Kraft was among those who said Macklemore would not be welcome at his Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, according to Macklemore and Sheeran. Macklemore further alleged Kraft “rallied” the other stadium owners to give Sheeran an ultimatum. Sheeran confirmed in a statement Tuesday that Kraft was among the venue representatives who’d reached out with concerns over Macklemore’s performance. Kraft did not deny Macklemore’s allegations when he gave a statement to NBC News on the matter. In his statement Monday, Kraft said he was not trying to stifle Palestinian advocacy or diminish the suffering of Palestinians. The decision, he said, was reached after comments Macklemore made at the tour’s New Jersey shows and “a broader history of rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.” “Much of my time and attention for the last decade has been focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed,” Kraft said. The NFL owner added that he agreed with Macklemore that there has been too much suffering, and noted that he has spent decades “directing resources” to Palestinians. “Standing with the Palestinian people and standing against Hamas, antisemitism and hate should not be mutually exclusive,” Kraft said. The backlash began earlier this month when Macklemore joined Sheeran’s tour at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Before performing “Hind’s Hall,” a protest anthem he released in 2024, he gave a speech to the crowd. According to video posted by Macklemore, he told the crowd that part of why he wanted to be on the tour was to be able to be in stadiums to say “Free Palestine.” He also made clear that his criticism of Israel’s government was not directed at people of Jewish faith. The clip drew controversy and criticism, including from fellow artist Pink, who is Jewish. She put out a statement Friday explaining why she reposted a social media post critical of Macklemore’s performance. Pink wrote she was not trying to get any artist fired or silence anyone, but that she took issue with Macklemore putting “violent images” of Israel’s military campaign in Gaza up in a stadium filled with families, then telling Jews in the audience that “it wasn’t about them.” Pink also referred a 2014 incident in which Macklemore wore a costume that appeared to play on antisemitic tropes: a wig, fake beard and hooked nose, worn to the Grammys that year. He said at the time he thought it would be fun to dress in disguise to talk to fans. Macklemore apologized after the antisemitic stereotype was pointed out, saying he’d been in touch with the Anti-Defamation League, an organization founded to combat antisemitism. The ADL accepted the apology at the time, saying it took him “at his word that he did not have any ill intent,” according to the Guardian. The organizations Macklemore says he will donate to are: Palestine Children’s Relief Fund, HEAL Palestine, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians, American Near East Refugee Aid (ANERA) and United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugee. He wrote that the donations are the least costly forms of solidarity and that his focus will remain on Palestinian people. Their right to freedom, dignity and safety is “what this has always been about,” Macklemore said. “When the news cycle moves on, which it will, don’t move with it,” he wrote. “Free Palestine.”

articles.title: Would-be Trump assassin Thomas Crooks had Snapchat, which may hold evidence 'treasure trove': former FBI agent
articles.summary: A Snapchat account tied to Thomas Crooks could hold a "treasure trove" of evidence, a retired FBI agent says, as Senate files reveal his digital trail.
articles.body: Newly released FBI files turned over to the Senate reveal a Snapchat account tied to Thomas Crooks, the man who attempted to assassinate President Donald Trump. The federal documents turned over to the Senate, first reported by the New York Post, revealed that FBI agents located a Snapchat account belonging to Crooks with the username "tom_crooks19." Crooks killed one person and seriously injured two others during his attempt to assassinate Trump July 13, 2024. According to the FBI documents, an Amazon account was also located. Crooks also had an account with Mailfence, an encrypted email service, which the documents say he logged into multiple times between April 15, 2024, and July 8, 2024. He also used a Gmail account. TWO YEARS AFTER BUTLER, THREATS AGAINST TRUMP KEEP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT IN SHARP FOCUS Retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent Jason Pack told Fox News Digital the Snapchat account may hold a "treasure trove" of evidence. "When you snap and that picture goes away that everything is gone, and that's not true. When I've served search warrants, there's been a treasure trove of information that has come back," Pack said. "It's not like some people think when you've snapped, and then it goes away, it's totally gone. That's not entirely the case." articles.title: Reporter for The Athletic fumes over Arch Manning, silent on Josh Jacobs' alleged violence against woman
articles.summary: The Athletic's Candace Buckner fumed over Arch Manning's AI video joke but has written nothing about Josh Jacobs' alleged strangulation charge.
articles.body: On Wednesday, The Athletic posted an op-ed fuming over Arch Manning and Steve Sarkisian. "Did Arch Manning, Steve Sarkisian and cackling reporters act this way? It can’t be real," Candace Buckner wrote in a headline. Buckner is referring to Manning citing an AI video earlier this week of Sarkisian slapping ESPN reporter Holly Rowe, which he and the reporters in the room found funny. On Saturday, Sarkisian blew up Rowe during a post-game interview. Manning has since apologized. Rowe said she accepted the apology. Evidently, Buckner did not. "I can’t tell which is worse: the phony clip depicting violence against a woman, or the real-life behavior displayed by Sarkisian, then Manning and a room of media members? Before they could edit themselves and add a glossy filter to their apologies, they showed the sordid bits of their individual characters for all to see," she wrote. For the record, Manning finding the AI-generated clip funny says nothing about his character. Even if you agree that he should have apologized – if, for nothing else, to mitigate the distraction – his comments are not worth the level of outrage Buckner is exhibiting. It's also notable that Buckner is showing such fury over Manning, Sarkisian, and reporters over their treatment of women, but not Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs. From what we can tell, Buckner has not penned a single article about Jacobs, who is facing a felony charge for allegedly strangling his ex-girlfriend. Not a word. Why is that? Why would a sports reporter for The Athletic show more disgust over a player joking about a meme hitting a woman than a player who was arrested and put on the NFL Commissioner's Exemption list for allegedly hitting women? We had hoped to find that answer. OutKick contacted The Athletic for comment and to see if we could speak to Candace Buckner for this article. The outlet did not respond. We will update this story if we hear from either The Athletic or Buckner. The Athletic's coverage disparity follows a familiar trend in sports media, in which reporters and commentators treat word crimes more seriously than violent crimes. For example, the usual suspects demanded similar accountability as Manning when Jaxon Dart introduced President Trump on stage and when Harrison Butker encouraged women to consider staying at home and raising kids. Likewise, they were as silent as they were with Jacobs when various players were arrested and charged with serious violent crimes, often against women.
